sources.title: 2026 NFL offseason newcomers impact ranking: draft, trades, signings
sources.notes: Fantasy-relevant offensive entries summarized from user-provided article text. Defensive-only entries were intentionally omitted from the fantasy journal.

facts.summary: New England acquired A.J. Brown, and Romeo Doubs also joined the Patriots receiving room.
Brown exceeded 1,000 receiving yards in each of his four seasons with Philadelphia.

outlook.summary: ESPN views Brown as a true No. 1 target for Drake Maye and sees Brown plus Doubs as a major upgrade to New England's receiver room.

facts.summary: Kyler Murray signed with Minnesota and ESPN identifies him as the likely starter.
Murray reached 20,000 passing yards and 3,000 rushing yards within his first seven NFL seasons.

outlook.summary: ESPN expects Kevin O'Connell to create more rhythm throws for Murray while continuing to use his rushing ability and isolating Justin Jefferson as a matchup target.

facts.summary: Denver acquired Jaylen Waddle from Miami.
Waddle averaged 14.2 yards per catch in 2025 and recorded 14 receptions of at least 20 yards.

outlook.summary: ESPN sees Waddle's route tree as a strong match for Bo Nix and expects him to add speed alongside Courtland Sutton.

facts.summary: Buffalo acquired DJ Moore from Chicago, and Joe Brady is the Bills' head coach.
Moore caught at least 90 passes in two of his three seasons with Chicago and had at least six receiving touchdowns in each of those three seasons.

outlook.summary: ESPN views Moore as Buffalo's explosive No. 1 receiver and projects him for more than 100 targets in 2026.

facts.summary: Arizona drafted Jeremiyah Love, who scored 21 total touchdowns for Notre Dame in 2025 and had 63 receptions during his college career.

outlook.summary: ESPN views Love as a potential three-down playmaker and expects his receiving route tree to expand in Arizona.

facts.summary: Mike Evans signed with San Francisco after injuries limited his 2025 production.
Evans reached 1,000 receiving yards in each of his first 11 NFL seasons.

outlook.summary: ESPN expects Evans to function as Kyle Shanahan's boundary X receiver and as an isolation/red-zone target for Brock Purdy.

facts.summary: Kenneth Walker III signed with Kansas City after the Chiefs averaged 4.2 yards per carry in 2025.
Walker recorded 33 rushes of at least 10 yards in 2025 and has had at least 25 receptions in every NFL season of his career.

outlook.summary: ESPN expects Walker's receiving skill to translate into Andy Reid's screen game and running-back route tree.

facts.summary: Houston added Braden Smith, Wyatt Teller and rookie Keylan Rutledge after finishing 2025 with the third-lowest pass block win rate.
Smith started 13 games at right tackle for Indianapolis in 2025 and improved his pass block win rate by seven percentage points from 2024.

outlook.summary: The personnel investment gives Houston a plausible path to better protection and blocking, which is a positive environment signal for Stroud and the run game but not a guarantee of improved fantasy output.

facts.summary: Malik Willis signed with Miami after appearing four times for Green Bay in 2025, including one start.
In those 2025 appearances, ESPN reports Willis completed 85.7% of his passes, rushed for 123 yards and scored four touchdowns.

outlook.summary: ESPN expects Bobby Slowik to use Willis as a dual-threat quarterback with designed runs, play action and vertical throws, while noting Miami is rebuilding.

facts.summary: New Orleans drafted Jordyn Tyson to join a receiver room led by Chris Olave and second-year quarterback Tyler Shough.

outlook.summary: ESPN expects Tyson to work opposite Olave and sees his vertical and middle-of-field ability as a fit in Kellen Moore's offense.

facts.summary: Isaiah Likely signed with the Giants after spending his Baltimore career behind Mark Andrews.

outlook.summary: ESPN calls Likely a breakout candidate and expects the Giants to scheme him targets at multiple levels, including screens and underneath outlets for Jaxson Dart.

facts.summary: Houston acquired David Montgomery after averaging 3.9 yards per carry in 2025.
Montgomery rushed for 33 touchdowns across his three seasons with Detroit.

outlook.summary: ESPN describes Montgomery as Houston's lead-role runner and emphasizes his low-red-zone production.

facts.summary: Alec Ingold signed with the Chargers to continue playing for Mike McDaniel after their time together in Miami.
ESPN reports Miami used 21 personnel on 234 snaps in 2025, the second-most in the NFL.

outlook.summary: Ingold's reunion with McDaniel is evidence of scheme continuity and more varied personnel usage in Los Angeles. That may create favorable motion/matchup opportunities, but it does not by itself prove higher target volume for McConkey.

facts.summary: A.J. Brown is no longer in Philadelphia, and the Eagles drafted Makai Lemon.

outlook.summary: ESPN expects Lemon to step into the No. 2 receiver role opposite DeVonta Smith under new coordinator Sean Mannion.

facts.summary: Seattle drafted Jadarian Price into a backfield that also includes George Holani, Emanuel Wilson and Zach Charbonnet, with Charbonnet returning from an ACL tear.

outlook.summary: ESPN sees Price as having traits to emerge early, but explicitly expects a shared-touch backfield.

facts.summary: Las Vegas signed Kirk Cousins and drafted Fernando Mendoza first overall; Cousins previously worked with coach Klint Kubiak in Minnesota.

outlook.summary: ESPN expects Cousins to open as the starter while Mendoza develops, creating a likely in-season quarterback transition risk for Raiders skill players.

facts.summary: Baltimore rebuilt the interior offensive line and drafted Olaivavega Ioane in the first round.

outlook.summary: ESPN sees Ioane as a fit for Declan Doyle's wide-zone scheme and as a player who can help keep the pocket firm for Lamar Jackson.

facts.summary: Tennessee drafted Carnell Tate and added Wan'Dale Robinson around second-year quarterback Cam Ward.

outlook.summary: ESPN expects Tate to separate in one-on-one matchups and become available to Ward at multiple levels, while Robinson adds target competition.

facts.summary: The Jets acquired Geno Smith after he threw a league-high 17 interceptions for Las Vegas in 2025.
New York's supporting cast includes Garrett Wilson, rookie Omar Cooper Jr. and rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq.

outlook.summary: ESPN believes Smith has a stronger supporting cast in New York and could stabilize the offense if his decision-making improves.

facts.summary: Chig Okonkwo signed with Washington after catching 56 passes for Tennessee in 2025.

outlook.summary: ESPN expects Okonkwo and rookie Antonio Williams to improve Jayden Daniels' middle-of-field passing options, with Okonkwo creating favorable interior matchups.

facts.summary: Travis Etienne Jr. signed with New Orleans, while the Saints restructured Alvin Kamara's contract to keep him on the roster.
Etienne scored 13 total touchdowns for Jacksonville in 2025.

outlook.summary: ESPN likes Etienne's receiving and perimeter-run fit in Kellen Moore's offense but explicitly notes Kamara will limit Etienne's total volume.

facts.summary: Las Vegas drafted Fernando Mendoza first overall and signed Kirk Cousins.

outlook.summary: ESPN expects Mendoza to play at some point in 2026 and views Klint Kubiak's system as a fit for on-time throws, play action, boots and vertical shots.

facts.summary: FantasyPros lists Darnold as an ADP faller and cites a run-heavy offensive environment as a fantasy-ceiling concern.

outlook.summary: The concern is fantasy passing volume rather than necessarily poor real-life quarterback play.
